text:
Connor Murphy came to Edmonton with a reputation earned over 547 games in Chicago: a big right-shot defenseman whose game is taking chances away. Evolving-Hockey backs that up. Last season it rated him 56th among 215 defensemen, with opponents getting 0.19 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on the ice (94th percentile), despite weak teammates.

That reputation is being tested. He's playing almost 21 minutes a night and blocking everything (45 shots in 18 games), but the Oilers have had only 38% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, more than 16 points worse than without him. It isn't bad luck, either: the goals have roughly matched the chances.

The points have dried up too. He's pointless in 13 straight on 2.6 expected, and the chances have thinned out. Our hunch is that his minutes are the thing to watch: on a team trying to win now, a defensive defenseman who isn't suppressing chances is hard to keep in the top four. Our projection still has him at about 15 points the rest of the way.
headline: Connor Murphy's defensive reputation is being tested
